# OpenLog

> A free training log that runs in the browser, keeps everything on the device
> and needs no account. It records lifts, runs, climbs, timed holds, bodyweight
> and body measurements, session by session.

OpenLog is a progressive web app at openlog.fit. It installs to a phone's home
screen from the browser, with no app store, and works offline once visited. The
log is held in the browser's own storage; there is no server-side account and
no analytics, and the data leaves only as a backup file the user exports. The
single exception is the optional AI plan builder: text pasted into it is sent
to OpenAI to turn a written programme into trackers, and is not stored.

It is deliberately not a coaching product. There are no feeds, streaks, charts
or progress graphs. What an exercise card shows is the numbers from the last
session, so the next set has something to beat.

## Model

Four levels, and no deeper. A **group** is a training day or a theme ("Friday",
"Body & cardio"). A **tracker** is a thing logged inside it: an exercise, a run,
a measurement. A tracker holds **variants**, which are alternatives that can be
swapped to when a machine is taken, each keeping its own numbers. An **entry**
is one logged set or reading.

A tracker's type is chosen once, from seven presets, and decides what an entry
looks like: strength (weight and reps), reps only, hold (time), cardio
(distance and time), body measure (length), bodyweight (weight), and count.

## Pages

- [Home](https://openlog.fit/): what it does, how logging works, how to install it.
- [App](https://openlog.fit/app/): the log itself. It opens by offering to build a plan, take a programme the user already follows, restore a backup, or start empty.
- [Privacy](https://openlog.fit/privacy/): what leaves the device, which is close to nothing.
- [Terms](https://openlog.fit/terms/)

## Notes

- Free. No paid tier, no ads, no sign-up.
- Metric and imperial can be switched at any time. Values are stored in one canonical unit, so switching rewrites nothing.
- A log moves between devices as a single exported JSON file. An import replaces what is on the receiving device rather than merging into it.
- Sessions can be backdated, so a workout written down the next morning still lands on the right day.
- Run by Yan Sokalau. Contact: openlog.fit@gmail.com
